title: Rubondo Island: A Park in Lake Victoria
excerpt: Rubondo Island lies in Lake Victoria and is a national park in its own right: forest, sitatunga antelopes, birds and peace.
body:
Rubondo Island National Park is an island in the southwest of Lake Victoria. It is one of Tanzania's least visited parks, and one of the most peaceful.

## Nature

Most of the island is covered in forest. The shoreline has papyrus, beaches and rocky inlets.

## Wildlife

- Sitatunga, an antelope adapted to swamps.
- Hippos and crocodiles along the shore.
- Many birds, including fish eagles, kingfishers and herons.
- Introduced species such as elephants and giraffes, brought to the island in past decades.
- A chimpanzee population introduced in the 1960s; tracking can be possible but they are not fully habituated.

## Activities

Forest walks, boat trips, fishing (with a permit) and birdwatching.

## Getting there

By light aircraft, or by road and boat via Mwanza or the Western Serengeti.

## Who it suits

Repeat visitors, birders and anyone who wants a few days in nature without crowds. See [your second safari](/blog/second-safari-ideas/).

Read our [Rubondo page](/national-parks/rubondo-island-national-park/) or [plan your trip](/travel-proposal/).
